docRequirement: headless.md binds the `--output-format stream-json` stream to a `system/init` frame that is "the first event in the stream unless startup events precede it" and carries `plugins` (each with `name` and `path`), `plugin_errors` (each with `plugin`, `type`, `message`; "Affected plugins are demoted and absent from `plugins`. The key is omitted when there are no errors"), `mcp_servers` (each with `name` and `status`), `mcp_server_errors` (each with `name`, `type`, `message`; `type` a skip category such as `unknown_type`, `url_missing_type`, `invalid_config`, `reserved_name`; "Affected servers are absent from `mcp_servers`. The key is omitted when there are no errors, so a CI gate can fail on a non-empty array"), and an optional `capabilities` string array. It also binds a `system/api_retry` frame (`attempt`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status`, `error`, `uuid`, `session_id`) before each retryable API retry. The page states that when a CI runner captures stderr, Claude Code prints no startup warning and "reports the skipped entries only in the `mcp_server_errors` field" — so the stream is the ONLY channel for that state.
current: Our headless stream is our own protocol, passed through verbatim. `sendAndStream` sets `const streamJson = args.outputFormat === 'stream-json'` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:457) and, inside the `client.on('session:event', ...)` subscription, writes each event as-is: `if (streamJson) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n') }` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:468-470). Nothing is written before the first server event — the CLI goes straight from `sessions:create` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:842-847) to `sessions:sendMessage` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:545-551), so there is no init frame of any spelling. The event union has no member for it: `AgentEvent` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966-1016) and the wire DTO `SessionEvent` (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:343-413) contain no `system`/`init` member and no member carrying a plugin or MCP load failure. There is no retry frame either — the only retry surface is free text: `yield { type: 'info', message: 'Retrying with fallback model ...' }` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6335-6339), and `grep -ran 'retry' packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts` returns nothing. The DATA behind three of the four documented arrays already exists server-side but never reaches the stream: `ResolvedInstalledPlugin` carries `name`, `version` and a server-only `bundleRootPath` "stripped from safe views" (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:675-709); `dependencyErrors` is already omitted-when-empty and already forces demotion (`resolver.ts:697-703`, projected at packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:415-422 as `{code, dependency, message}`); the demoting load diagnostics `plugin.user_config.unset`, `plugin.app.connector_unresolved`, `plugin.mcp.required_environment_missing` are built at packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1870-1908; live MCP state is `McpPoolHealth {status, connected, failed}` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:322-326, computed at :1686-1702) and rides only the Pi harness snapshot (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3105, :3178; packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:315), reachable over `sessions:getPiHarnessRuntime` (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:44) which apps/cli never calls. The fourth array has no producer at all: an MCP source whose `config.json` is unparsable or carries no recognised `type` is silently retained with `sourceType` undefined and no diagnostic (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:558-568). The only CI gate we do ship is out of band: `nessy-general-agent doctor --json` exits 1 and emits `unfulfilledPluginMandates`, `invalidManagedEntries`, `rejectedSettingsLayers`, `invalidAgentDefinitions` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:184-232) — mandated-but-not-installed only, nothing about an installed plugin that failed to load and nothing about MCP servers. Our CLI also has no `--mcp-config` and no `--plugin-dir` flag (flag switch, apps/cli/src/index.ts:80-157).
divergence: The `system/init` frame does not exist, so all four CI-gating arrays (`plugins`, `plugin_errors`, `mcp_servers`, `mcp_server_errors`) and the optional `capabilities` array are absent from the headless stream, as is `system/api_retry`. This is a missing frame, not a key-name mismatch: there is no member of any spelling on `AgentEvent`/`SessionEvent` carrying plugin or MCP load state. Two sub-deltas differ in nature and must not be treated alike. (1) `plugin_errors` is a PROJECTION gap — the demotion set is already computed and already omitted-when-empty (`ResolvedInstalledPlugin.dependencyErrors`, resolver.ts:697-703, plus the three demoting diagnostics at resolver.ts:1870-1908); only the key names differ (`code` vs `type`, plugin `name` vs `plugin`) and no frame carries it. Likewise `plugins[].path`: the value exists as `bundleRootPath` (resolver.ts:709) and is deliberately stripped from the Safe view, so it needs a new non-Safe projection, not a Safe-view change. (2) `mcp_server_errors` is a MISSING PRODUCER — nothing anywhere records an MCP server skipped for invalid config; native-sources.ts:562-566 swallows the parse failure. `mcp_servers[].status` is half-present: `McpPoolHealth.connected/failed` gives per-slug status but only after the Pi runtime has started, which is after the first turn, i.e. after the point the doc puts the init frame. `capabilities` is the weakest binding of the set — the page says the field "requires Claude Code v2.1.205 or later and is absent from earlier versions", so a consumer must tolerate its absence; we also have no protocol-capability names to put in it (`grep -ran 'interrupt_receipt' packages apps` → 0 hits). Two items in the original claim's enumeration are NOT divergences and stay out of the fix: the stream does terminate (`complete`, dto.ts:351, handled at apps/cli/src/index.ts:516-535) and that frame does carry cost (`TokenUsage.costUsd`, packages/core/src/types/message.ts:500-505) — only the spelling `total_cost_usd` differs.

blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary twice, which is a risk trigger in this repo. (1) The new RPC channel touches packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts and the routing allowlist in packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts; any channel not in that allowlist is unreachable, and the electron transport map (apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts:224 pattern) is where a renderer consumer would have to be added if one is ever wanted. (2) The `api_retry` half adds a member to `AgentEvent` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966) and `SessionEvent` (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:343) — both are consumed by the electron renderer's `session:event` handling and by the CLI passthrough, and every exhaustive switch over the union must tolerate it. Note the validator trap on the neighbouring path: packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:100 asserts an EXACT key set on the harness snapshot (`exact(input, [… 'mcpHealth' …])`), so if a fixer chooses to extend the harness snapshot instead of adding the new channel, that allowlist and the `mcpHealth` validator at :177 must be updated or validation throws. The capability-resolver edits are read by everything that consumes `EffectiveCapabilitySnapshot`: toUserCatalog / toSafeInstalledPlugin (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:382-498, the renderer catalog), the materializer (packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:86, :241), runtime-output-styles.ts:24, and the capabilities RPC surface (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/capabilities.ts, with its test suite at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/__tests__/capabilities.test.ts). The path-free invariant on `SafeInstalledPluginSummary` (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:289-320, 'Names/status only; no paths, commands, URLs or secret refs' at :880) is the boundary that must NOT be relaxed to obtain `plugins[].path` — a Safe-view change would leak bundle paths to the renderer. Imported-plugin paths matter here: the demoted-plugin set the frame reports comes from `plugin-dependencies` resolution over Claude- and Codex-format bundles, so both format adapters feed it. No persistence boundary is crossed: the init frame is derived, nothing new is written to disk.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. Today `nessy-general-agent run --output-format stream-json` in CI emits only our own turn events — the first line is a `text_delta`/`tool_start`, never metadata — so a pipeline cannot tell which model, which plugins or which MCP servers the run actually had. When an installed plugin is demoted (unsatisfied declared dependency, missing required MCP env var, unset `user_config` key — the states resolver.ts:697-703 and :1870-1908 already compute) or an MCP source fails to connect or has a malformed `config.json`, the run proceeds with those tools and skills simply absent, prints a plausible answer, and exits 0. The CI job goes green on a degraded agent: a Bash-guard `PreToolUse` hook that never loaded is the worst case, because the gate the pipeline believes it has is not running. The desktop control center CAN see degraded MCP state (`mcpHealth {status, connected, failed}`, SessionManager.ts:3178) — the headless surface cannot, so the same failure is visible in the GUI and invisible in CI. Partial workaround a user has today: run `nessy-general-agent doctor --json` as a separate step, which exits 1 on `unfulfilledPluginMandates` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:219-222) — it covers mandated-but-not-installed only, not an installed plugin that failed to load, and nothing about MCP servers.
notes: Scope note: f180's claim is about the CI-gating fields, so `system/plugin_install` (documented in the same section, gated on `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL`) is adjacent and deliberately left out of the change list — we have no pre-turn marketplace install phase to report. Ordering constraint a fixer will hit: the doc puts `system/init` first in the stream, but live MCP connection status (`McpPoolHealth`) only exists once the Pi runtime has started, which is after the first send (`unavailableReason: 'pi-runtime-not-started'`, packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:304 / SessionManager.ts:3163-3164). So `mcp_servers[].status` at init time can only be a configured/credential-ready status, not a connected one; `mcp_server_errors` (config-validation skips) is unaffected because it is computed at inventory time, which is exactly why the doc's CI gate hangs on that array rather than on status. One inherited item: the absence of ANY other stream member carrying a plugin or MCP load failure (the `info`/`status` events cover mirror errors, hook errors, compaction, fallback-model retry and agent eviction) is the challenger's verified check; I confirmed the two union definitions myself (message.ts:966-1016, dto.ts:343-413) and spot-checked pi-agent.ts:6325-6343, but did not re-enumerate every `info` emission site.
